subject: SLA evidence acceptance criteria & probe harmonization (RFP reply)
messages:
From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@healthtech.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthtech.com
Date: 2027-04-11T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Clarifications on SLA evidence & probe harmonization for RFP

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the draft RFP responses you sent earlier. Our procurement and SRE teams reviewed the SLA / measurement sections and we have a few clarifying questions before we finalize the scoring:

1) Evidence acceptance: can you list the exact artifacts Redwood expects to provide as "evidence" for uptime/latency measurements (e.g., raw probe logs, aggregated percentiles, per-region buckets, trace ids)? What formats do you accept (CSV, Parquet, XLSX)?

2) Measurement windows and clock alignment: do you measure windows in UTC? How do you handle clock skew across regions and probe hosts when attributing an outage?

3) Synthetic probes vs production telemetry: will Redwood rely solely on synthetic probing for SLA calculations, or will you combine synthetic and sampled production traces? If combined, how are they weighted?

4) Service credit trigger: please provide a short description of the credit calculation (example: how a p99 latency breach over a 1-hour window maps to a percentage credit). Also confirm what counts as a valid "customer-impacting" incident.

5) Audit access: in the event of a dispute, are raw traces and logs (with timestamps and request ids) available for audit? What is the retention period for telemetry used for SLA adjudication?

Can you respond with a concise acceptance criteria checklist we can attach to the procurement packet? If possible, include a sample probe cadence and sample sizes per region.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our internal deadline is EOD 2027-04-14.

Best,
Maria Garcia
Procurement Lead, HealthTech Inc.
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarifications on SLA evidence & probe harmonization for RFP

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list of items. Below is a concise acceptance checklist plus answers to each of your questions. I attached a pre-filled evidence template (redwood-sla-evidence-template.xlsx) and a sample probe schedule (probe-schedule.csv) to make integration easier.

Acceptance checklist (one-page summary):
- Evidence artifacts: aggregated percentile CSVs (p50/p90/p95/p99), raw synthetic probe logs (CSV), per-region rollups (CSV/XLSX), request-id trace samples (Parquet/JSONL)
- Formats accepted: CSV, XLSX for bundles; Parquet/JSONL for raw trace exports
- Windowing: UTC-aligned 1-hour windows for primary adjudication; 24-hour rollups for monthly SLOs
- Probe cadence: default 1 probe / region / 30s (configurable per customer); see attached CSV for examples
- Sample size: default probe population yields ~120k probes/day/region; production-sampled traces targeted at 0.1%-1% sampling depending on throughput
- Attribution: incidents attributable to Redwood are those where (a) synthetic probe failures exceed configured threshold in at least two availability zones in the same region within the window, or (b) production error rate correlated with probe failures and traced to Redwood-serving layer
- Credit calc (summary): credits are computed per affected region per window; baseline formula: credit_pct = min(100, floor((breach_ms / threshold_ms) * scaling_factor)) applied to region-weighted monthly bill; exact table included in the attached template
- Audit access & retention: telemetry used for adjudication retained 90 days by default; raw trace export available on request for disputes (see below)

Answers to your numbered questions:
1) Artifacts & formats: see checklist. We will supply both aggregated reports and raw probe logs. Request-id level traces delivered as compressed Parquet or JSONL when requested.

2) Windowing & clock skew: we align measurement windows to UTC. Probe hosts are NTP-synchronized; we record clock offset per probe in the logs and use server-side timestamps as the source of truth for adjudication. For skew >200ms we flag events and exclude skewed probes from the primary aggregation after manual review.

3) Synthetic vs production telemetry: by default we use synthetic probes for availability/uptime SLOs and production-sampled traces for latency SLOs. We support combined metrics on request — weighting is agreed in the contract (default: synthetic 70% / production 30% for latency).

4) Service credit trigger & formula: the attached spreadsheet includes a credit matrix. Short version: breaches measured at p99 over the 1-hour window that exceed the threshold by X% map to tiered credits (0.5% / 1% / 2.5% of monthly bill for tier levels 1/2/3). Credits are region-weighted and capped per contract.

5) Audit access & retention: raw traces are available for audits via a secured, time-limited S3 export (Parquet+manifest). Standard retention 90 days; extended retention available as an add-on. Exports include UTC timestamps, probe/request ids, region/az labels, and any measured clock offset.

Next steps / ask from HealthTech:
- Confirm whether you want per-region weighting (default is equal weighting across your active regions)
- Confirm desired probe cadence (we can reduce to 1/min or increase to 1/10s for critical regions)
- Confirm whether production traces are permitted for weighting (we require a data-processing addendum for trace export)

CC'ing Karthik and Laura — Karthik will follow up with the credit matrix language for the MSA. Laura can help map the probe schedule to your SRE topology.

Regards,

Olga Petrov
Senior Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood-sla-evidence-template.xlsx (XLSX), probe-schedule.csv (CSV)

Hi Maria — looping in answers inline and a couple of concrete next steps.

On Tue, Apr 12, 2027 at 08:21 Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@healthtech.com> wrote:
> - Telemetry fields: can you provide an explicit list of required telemetry fields for the raw export (we need to map them to our SIEM and retention policy)?

Answered: standard export schema (we'll provide a manifest with the Parquet):
- event_timestamp_utc
- region
- availability_zone
- probe_id
- probe_type (synthetic/production_sample)
- request_id (if present)
- latency_ms
- status_code / error_class
- backend_cluster_id
- server_timestamp
- client_clock_offset_ms
- trace_sample (boolean)
- sampling_rate_pct

These fields are sufficient to reconstruct per-window aggregates and to support forensic tracebacks.

> - Private deployment impact: does the evidence collection change if we move to a private (VPC) deployment, or will Redwood still operate the probe fleet for SLA adjudication?

Answered: measurement methodology remains the same. For VPC/private deployments we have two options: (1) Redwood-managed external probes from public points-of-presence and synthetic probes launched by Redwood agents inside the VPC (agent binaries subject to your security review), or (2) customer-managed probe agents that push signed logs to our adjudication pipeline. Either option is contractually captured; default is Redwood-managed probes with agent optional.

> - Time sync & offset recording

Answered: probes must be NTP-synchronized; we record client_clock_offset_ms per probe and include it in manifests. Any probe with offset >200ms is flagged; such probes are excluded from automatic adjudication and routed to a manual review queue.

Pricing/retention notes: 12-month retention is available as an add-on; I will have pricing from Finance in a separate doc.

Next steps (proposed):
- Olive branch: we will upload a completed "SLA evidence acceptance checklist" to the HubSpot deal and to the shared Drive by EOD 2027-04-14. (Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C)
- Schedule a 30-minute SRE alignment call to confirm region list, probe cadence, and traffic weights. Proposed slots: 2027-04-15 09:30-10:00 PT or 2027-04-16 14:00-14:30 PT.
- If HealthTech prefers, we can include a short MPA addendum to the MSA that lists the exact telemetry fields, probe cadence, and credit matrix. I attached a draft mutual action plan (redwood-mutual-action-plan.pdf) for your review.

Action items:
- HealthTech: confirm preferred call slot and provide region traffic split sample
- Redwood: upload finalized checklist and pricing for 12-month retention

Happy to jump on a call this week — thanks for moving quickly, Maria.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Reliability & Escalations, Redwood Inference
